title: Cytochrome c oxidase assay
author: Wen Aw
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.shieb4e

steps.title: Homogenize larvae in buffer
steps.instruction: Grind third instar larvae for 10 s in 100 µL ice‑cold homogenization buffer (50 mM phosphate, 0.05 % Tween‑80) using a Kontes pellet pestle motor.

steps.title: Dilute homogenate
steps.instruction: Add an additional 500 µL of the same homogenization buffer to the homogenate, mixing to a total volume of 600 µL.

steps.title: Centrifuge to remove debris
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the samples at 2000 g for 5 min at 4 °C to pellet cell debris.

steps.title: Aliquot supernatant into plate
steps.instruction: Dilute the cleared supernatant 1 : 10, then pipette 40 µL of this diluted supernatant into each of six wells of a 96‑well plate.

steps.title: Add reduced cytochrome c
steps.instruction: At the time of assay, add 160 µL of reduced cytochrome c (50 µM) to each well.

steps.title: Add control and measure protein
steps.instruction: Include a no‑cytochrome c control well; determine the protein concentration of each sample using the Bio‑Rad DC Protein Assay method.

steps.title: Read plate in microplate reader
steps.instruction: Place the plate in a Molecular Devices SpectraMax 384 Plus microplate reader and record absorbance at 550 nm every 10 s for 5 min.

steps.title: Calculate Vmax from slope
steps.instruction: Oxidation of cytochrome c is indicated by a decline in OD at 550 nm (extinction coefficient = 29.5). Use the maximum slope of the OD‑versus‑time plot, calculated by the reader, as Vmax for the reaction.
